executive_summary.question: Under what circumstances does the right of private defence of the body NOT extend to voluntarily causing the assailant's death?
executive_summary.generated_answer:
The right of private defence of the body **does not** extend to voluntarily causing the assailant’s death in the following situations:

- **When the offence is not one of the specific descriptions listed in § 38** – i.e., when the assault does **not** reasonably cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt, and is not:  
  - an assault with intent to commit rape,  
  - an assault with intent to gratify unnatural lust,  
  - an assault with intent to kidnap or abduct,  
  - an assault with intent to wrongfully confine a person under circumstances where the person cannot resort to public authorities, or  
  - an act of throwing/administering acid that may reasonably cause apprehension of grievous hurt.  
  *(See § 39: “If the offence be not of any of the descriptions specified in section 38, the right of private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death …”)*【90f8747a-7f40-4ae3-b114-2b216129f432】

- **When the act does not reasonably cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt** – even if the act is an offence, the right to cause death is unavailable. This is reinforced by the general limitation in § 37(2) that the right never extends to inflicting more harm than necessary for defence.  
  *(See § 37(2): “The right of private defence in no case extends to the inflicting of more harm than it is necessary to inflict for the purpose of defence.”)*【6f639d07-62fa-48e0-a811-5492ff51880e】

- **When the act is done by a public servant (or under his direction) in good faith and does not reasonably cause apprehension of death or grievous hurt** – § 37(1)(a) and (b) expressly deny the right of private defence in such cases.  
  *(See § 37(1)(a)–(b) in the context of public‑servant acts.)*【69db30c9-72ad-48eb-b310-9e3137806fa2】

- **When there is time to seek protection from the public authorities** – § 37(1)(c) removes the right of private defence if the defender could have recourse to public protection.  
  *(See § 37(1)(c).)*【69db30c9-72ad-48eb-b310-9e3137806fa2】

In summary, the right to voluntarily cause death is unavailable unless the assault falls under one of the grave categories enumerated in § 38 (death, grievous hurt, rape, unnatural lust, kidnapping, wrongful confinement without recourse, or acid‑attack causing apprehension of grievous hurt) and the other restrictions of § 37 (necessity, no public‑servant good‑faith exception, and availability of public authorities) are satisfied. If any of those conditions is missing, the right extends only to causing non‑lethal harm.

evidence_analysis.claim_text: The right of private defence of the body does not extend to voluntarily causing the assailant’s death when the offence is not one of the specific descriptions listed in § 38.
evidence_analysis.supporting_evidence:
If the offence be not of any of the descriptions specified in section 38, the right of
private defence of the body does not extend to the voluntary causing of death to the
assailant, but does extend, under the restrictions specified in section 37, to the voluntary
causing to the assailant of any harm other than death.
